channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: AI Emerges as a Flashpoint in Trump-Xi Talks
item.description: The US-China AI race is emerging as a key issue surrounding talks between President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping, as Chinese open-weight models close the gap with leading US systems. Rhodium Group’s Reva Goujon discusses tensions over AI safety and export controls, divisions within the Trump administration over potential guardrails, and how technology restrictions, critical minerals and Taiwan factor into the broader US-China negotiations. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta Bets on AI, Devices for Its Next Chapter
item.description: Meta is experimenting with new ways to move beyond its social media roots, from the fast-growing Muse AI assistant to smart glasses and its new palm-sized Charm device. eMarketer Senior Analyst Minda Smiley discusses whether Muse marks a turning point for Meta’s AI strategy, why the company is testing multiple hardware form factors, and whether its latest products have staying power or risk becoming another short-lived technology fad. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Dutch Prime Minister Has Discussed MATCH Act With Trump
item.description: Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten had discussions on legislation which would further restrict ASML Holding NV’s sales in China with President Donald Trump. Jetten told Bloomberg Television, “I’m pretty sure we come to some agreement that is workable for each and every one.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Texas Attorney General Probes Data Center Projects Over Water Usage
item.description: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton is investigating hundreds of data center developments over whether they’re complying with water-use reporting requirements.
item.dc:creator: Julia Amann and Joe Lovinger

item.title: HouseCanary Files Bankruptcy to Collect $260 Million From Rocket
item.description: Property data provider HouseCanary Inc. filed for bankruptcy to buy time to collect more than $260 million from affiliates of Rocket Mortgage, which were accused of stealing a computer model used to quickly value homes for real estate investors and mortgage brokers.
item.dc:creator: Steven Church

item.title: Meta Introduces Palm-Sized Device to Use Muse AI on the Go
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. unveiled a palm-sized, dedicated gadget for using Muse, the company’s popular new artificial intelligence assistant, pushing deeper into the AI devices market with a surprise announcement. Bloomberg's Mandeep Singh joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump-Xi Summit, Oracle Buildout Hits New Hurdle
item.description: A global bond rout sends the 30-year yield to a 22-year high. President Trump and China President Xi meet today after extending the US, China trade truce. Elizabeth Economy breaks down Washington’s fading leverage over Beijing. Plus, oil surges as tensions with Iran escalate. And tech billionaire Vinod Khosla joins us on why America can’t slow the AI race. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: BNP Paribas CIB Strikes AI Deal with Google Cloud, Credit Memo/Res
item.description: BNP Paribas SA is deepening its partnership with Alphabet Inc.’s Google Cloud, extending it for a five-year period as the bank is counting on artificial intelligence to increase efficiency.
item.dc:creator: Claudia Cohen

item.title: The Biggest AI Adoption RIsk
item.description: Former Instacart President and current Beacon CEO Nilam Ganenthiran says the biggest obstacle to AI adoption is trust. He explains why AI is “arming both the good guys and bad guys,” how safety fears are holding back the real economy, and why Beacon is building what he calls an “AI-native Berkshire Hathaway.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Leverage Over China Is Fading: Economy
item.description: Elizabeth Economy, a former Biden administration China adviser and a senior fellow at the Hoover Institution, joins Bloomberg Open Interest to break down what could emerge from US-China talks beyond the diplomatic spectacle. She sees potential cooperation on AI security, but warns Washington’s traditional leverage is weakening. From Iranian oil and semiconductor controls to rare earths and trade commitments, Economy argues the US will increasingly need allies to pressure Beijing. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tech Industry ‘Fumbled’ AI Messaging, Vinod Khosla Says
item.description: Billionaire venture capitalist Vinod Khosla said AI development shouldn’t slow down, while also acknowledging that the tech industry has hurt itself with poor messaging.
item.dc:creator: Erika Tulfo

item.title: AI Evaluators Raise Ideological Bias Concern for Trump, Industry
item.description: Groups that perform the niche work of assessing artificial intelligence models have suddenly found themselves at the center of a global debate over safety that could shape the pace of AI innovation and the direction of financial markets.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Eastland and Rachel Metz

item.title: Oracle Cites ‘Force Majeure’ to Seek Cover From Data Center Delays
item.description: Oracle sent a notice citing force majeure to the project's developer, a unit of Blue Owl Capital Inc., regarding a massive data center being built in New Mexico. Sridhar Natarajan reports on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Khosla: America Can’t Slow AI
item.description: Vinod Khosla, an early investor of OpenAI and the founder of Khosla Ventures, says slowing AI development could hand China a strategic advantage. He joined Bloomberg Open Interest to argue that America should accelerate AI and energy infrastructure while protecting workers displaced by automation, not their individual jobs. He also says Silicon Valley has failed to clearly communicate AI’s potential benefits in healthcare, education and economic growth. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ex-Tinder Exec Debuts Rivet, a Dating App That Lets Strangers Play Matchmaker
item.description: A former Tinder executive launched a new dating app that invites the community to vote on strangers’ compatibility, putting a twist on courtship at a time when singles have grown exhausted with swiping.Rivet, which opens to US users on Thursday, relies on a pool of volunteer “matchers” who rate whether two given people might be compatible. The idea is to prioritize quality connections over quantity, giving daters just a few pre-vetted options at a time, founder and Chief Executive Officer Taru K
item.dc:creator: Samantha Kelly

item.title: US Stock Futures Today: Darden, Dropbox, Everpure, MGM Resorts
item.description: S&P 500 Index futures are down 0.6% as of 7:44 a.m. in New York after fresh gains in oil prices fueled further selling in bonds and lifted 30-year Treasury yields to the highest since 2004.
item.dc:creator: Will Daley

item.title: Qualcomm Renews Licensing Pact With Apple Starting in 2027
item.description: Qualcomm Inc., the largest producer of smartphone processors, renewed its global licensing pact with Apple Inc. starting April 1, signaling that the iPhone maker will remain a customer for now.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Frier and Nick Turner

item.title: Pharmacy Benefits Firm Rightway Eyes IPO After New Funding
item.description: Rightway, an upstart pharmacy benefit manager covering about 3 million people, is considering an initial public offering in the years ahead as it tries to chip away at a market long dominated by some of the largest healthcare conglomerates in the US.
item.dc:creator: Ike Swetlitz

item.title: BlackRock, IFM Close In on $25 Billion Asia Data Center Deal
item.description: A consortium backed by BlackRock Inc. and IFM Investors Pty has entered exclusive talks for a potential acquisition of Stack Infrastructure Inc.’s Asia Pacific data centers, people familiar with the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Baigorri and Elffie Chew

item.title: Meta Debuts Dedicated Muse Charm Gadget for AI Assistant Users
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. unveiled a palm-sized, dedicated gadget for using Muse, the company’s popular new artificial intelligence assistant, pushing deeper into the AI devices market with a surprise announcement.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman
